# Review - PR 577 @ 3d18d4fe3535b5c05cebe82d7eb1b1ca2c7d34a7

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: `43466f544a129fdf72cd90e7769f1e139b027fe1` (`github/main`). Four files, +331 / -28 against merge base `76345a0251444dcafad1415b033b72f58b6511e0`: the merge subject's cosmetic `[lean +A -D]` bracket now counts Lean *code* lines only, with the matching protocol text and workflow tests; no Lean source, blueprint TeX, paper-gap or audit file is touched, so no proof-integrity surface moves.

## Findings

- [x] F1 (code; minor) local/bin/pr_merge.py:713 - a Lean char literal holding a double quote (`def c : Char := '"'`) opens string state that never closes, so every later line of that blob is scored non-code: run against the head module, `lean_code_line_mask` returns `[True, False, False]` for that literal followed by two theorems. Same class as the earlier multiline-string finding, and the persistent string state widened it from one line to the file tail; non-blocking because no `*.lean` blob on `github/main` contains such a literal (640 files scanned with the head scanner; the only long uncounted tail, `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree.lean`, is a genuine module docstring) and the number is cosmetic by contract. A `'` + `"` + `'` guard, or one sentence at :674 recording the new blast radius, would close it.
- [x] F2 (code; minor) local/bin/pr_merge.py:665 - the docstring defines a code line as one carrying a non-whitespace character outside every comment, but a continuation line inside an ordinary multiline string is returned `False` (`'def s := "a\nmiddle line\nend"'` gives `[True, False, False, True]`). scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py:1417 pins that behavior and neither the docstring nor the counting rule in local/protocols/issues-prs.md:172 mentions it; the choice is defensible for a size signal, the two descriptions should state it.
- [x] F3 (code; minor) local/bin/pr_merge.py:765 - the `-U0` blob diff passes `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` but not `--no-color`. With `color.ui=always` or `color.diff=always` in the operator's git config the hunk headers arrive ANSI-wrapped, `HUNK_HEADER_RE` matches nothing, and every modified file contributes 0 silently instead of the `None` fallback (reproduced on ghz: `git -c color.diff=always diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -U0 <blob> <blob>` prints `^[[36m@@ -2 +2 @@`). The `--raw -z` record walk at :791 is unaffected. Adding `--no-color` removes the exposure.

## Review

What I checked. The full main-relative change (`git diff 76345a02 3d18d4fe`) in all four files; the branch carries the original commit, the multiline-string repair `6d6128db`, and two merges of `github/main` that add nothing to the main-relative diff. Policy was read from `github/main` only: `local/personas/reviewer.md`, `local/personas/prose-reviewer.md`, `local/protocols/review.md`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` section 5 and the proof-integrity and faithful-statement sections of `AGENTS.md`.

The prior marked review of head `723e2d2a` left exactly one open finding: a multiline Lean string containing `/-` suppressed all later code lines. It is resolved at this head. String and escape state now persist across physical newlines until the closing quote (:698-:704), the reviewer's own counterexample returns `[True, False, True]`, the escaped-quote variant likewise, and `MergeSubjectTests` gained both a mask case and an end-to-end delta regression (`test_delta_counts_code_after_a_multiline_string_containing_comment_opener`, expecting `[lean +1 -1]`).

Measurement logic. The blob-id route is sound: `--raw -z --find-renames --no-abbrev` records are walked with the correct one- or two-path stride for R/C, a record that does not parse abandons the whole count, absent or non-blob modes yield an empty mask so added and deleted files take the natural branch, a pure rename is skipped on equal blob ids, a NUL-bearing blob counts nothing, removals are judged in the base blob and additions in the head blob, and `-U0` hunks with a zero count produce an empty range rather than a spurious line. The nesting depth counter handles `/-`, `/--` and `/-!` with the shared `-/` closer; a trailing `--` comment keeps its line; `n - -1` after code still counts. The new `_raw_diff_blob_pairs` is not redundant with the existing `_is_tolerated_telemetry_change` walk at :186, which is `--no-renames`, mode-exact and path-based by design. The cosmetic contract is respected and now explicit: `lean_line_delta` keeps its name, signature and `None`-on-anything behavior, nothing reads the number back, and no gate, CI step or REST key changes.

Verification. `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_github_workflow.MergeSubjectTests -v` in the PR worktree: 13 tests, OK (read-only; no source, index or build output touched). Exact-head status `gh api .../commits/3d18d4fe.../status`: `success`, with `local-ci/build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`, `blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`, `statement-origin` and `local-ci/summary` all green. I ran the head scanner over all 640 `*.lean` blobs of `github/main` looking for files whose tail it wrongly silences; none. Commit subjects follow `type(scope): short description` in the imperative under 72 characters, and the PR body has Motivation, Description and Testing.

Prose. The two changed documents are workflow protocol prose, not mathematical prose. `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` and the dated `EVOLUTION.md` entry describe what the code does — code lines only, comment and blank lines excluded, a trailed comment harmless, base-side classification for removals and head-side for additions, added/deleted/renamed files all counted, the scanner raising nothing and a failed measurement sending no wording — with the one gap recorded as F2. Both keep the issue #557 cosmetic rule intact and cite their owner-issue trigger.

Not checked: full CI or a full `lake build` (none needed, no Lean file changes); the repository-wide unit suite (the PR body reports 644 tests, 9 skipped, from the pre-commit hook); the real merge path against GitHub; the dry-run figures quoted in the PR body for merges of earlier packets; exotic or malformed Lean lexical forms beyond the cases above.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=APPROVED)
